question: The green revolution technology resulted in an increase in production of cereal production from 72.4 million tons in 1965-66 to _______ million tons in 1978-79.
solution:
The correct answer is __**131.9**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The green revolution is the rise in agricultural productivity, particularly in developing nations, made possible by the use of novel crops and farming techniques.
 
• Given that he started the Green Revolution in India, M. S. Swaminathan is regarded as its father. He was motivated by Norman Borlaug's effort.
 
• Norman Borlaug started the Green Revolution movement in the 1960s. He is referred to as the "Father of the Green Revolution" globally. For his efforts in creating High Yielding Varieties (HYVs) of wheat, it resulted in him being awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.
 
• In order to enhance food production and reduce hunger and poverty, high-yielding cultivars of rice and wheat were first introduced in India in the 1960s.
 
• In Punjab, the Green Revolution in India was first implemented in late 1966 or early 1967 as a part of a development initiative launched by international donor organisations and the Indian government.
 
• One of the innovative techniques created during the Green Revolution was drip irrigation. This technology allowed water to drop slowly and steadily to the roots of plants, saving water and promoting more sustainable agriculture.
 
• India has achieved significant progress thanks to the Green Revolution, which has brought about a previously unheard-of level of food security. It has helped many non-poor people avoid the poverty and hunger they would have otherwise faced while lifting a significant number of poor people out of poverty
